questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience what it was like to live in a completely different place.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a top uni and I wanted to go to a big city. Furthermore my options were rather limited as I had some mandatory courses for which I needed similar replacements.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy although HKU bombards you with information - often times the same information repeated in a different format.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The assistance is spares, but it is not that difficult to figure it out yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: You to be quite proactive in the first few days to establish a network of other students as the uni does leave a lot to be desired in regards to encourage social activity for the exchange students - but everybody is in the same boat so don't worry.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: You have to apply through the uni. It will all be laid out in the folder you receive when accepted to the uni. I recommend applying for on campus housing or the housing units in Jockey Club 3 placed in Kennedy Town. (these are called Chi Sun College, New College and two more, you can find them on reddit. Chi Sun is the best one).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Accept any offer you get through the uni. So far, UCPH students have always gotten an offer, but the students from other uni's that did not get an offer through the uni had to pay super high rents.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a roommate which of course was not ideal, but at the same time a great opportunity to get to know someone from a completely different culture.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You will be registered to a host faculty and need to do at least 50% of your credits there. The student administration is useless. It is not stated explicitly anywhere, but you can switch host faculty, you just need to choose 50% of your credits at the same faculty. (At least you can do this if your are from science).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Through their website. You need to get up at 4 AM CET to register a couple of weeks before you arrive, but other than that the process is fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None of note.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Success. Although no admin told me that I could switch faculty until after it was too late which forced me into some classes that I did not really want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get up early and register in early August. Try out a lot of classes in the add-drop period. Beware that all classes will have midterms even if they do not explicitly state so. My advice would be to get a mix of running evaluation and courses with finals. The courses with finals have a way higher workload.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The intellectual level was generally lower, but the workload was definitely higher and the exams were heavily speed and memory based which I found difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lower complexity, higher workload. Did sometimes feel very redundante. I prefer the teaching at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to optimization, Financial economics I, The Statistics of Investment Risk, Nature of the Universe , Programming Technologies.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Programming Technologies - it is a self-learning course in C++. You learn a lot and it is perfect for an exchange student. 
Introduction to optimization, Financial economics I and The Statistics of Investment Risk are all great courses, but I do not find the work to learning pay off worth it. Especially introduction to optimization is very difficult.

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None - I ate almost all my meals out as a great local meal will run you 50-70 DKK. So you could obviously reduce the meal-spending a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out. Club entrances are high and drinks are typically priced at CPH-nightclub prices - at bars as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the rowing team, but the rowing did not start until November.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The social activités are mostly geared towards full time students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Through CEDERS (the student org) I somehow got invited to a local family dinner for a festive gathering which was great. Every time you get the opportunity to interact with local cantonese you should really try to grab it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would defiantly recommend visiting Shenzhen, Taiwan and Macau, but other than that, stay in HK. I spent almost all my time in the city and still feel like I have only seen a fraction of the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Surprisingly difficult actually. I have traveled a lot and so expected it to be quite easy, but the extreme summer weather in Hong Kong along with the chaotic add-drop periode was a few dizzy weeks. You get into a routine pretty quickly though and again, everybody is in the same boat.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not have a lot of success with this, but joining a sports team is my best bet and where I found a tiny bit of success.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Doom scrolling.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fast pace.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Use the add-drop periode, be very open in the first week, eat out as much as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The whole thing about the possibility of switch host faculty ahaha. And beware of how great a difference the workload can be in different courses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to feel at home in another city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing important people at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
